description:
The subculture was characterized by zealous fandom for traditional popular music (especially the crooning of Frank Sinatra) and pioneering a new, peer-oriented casual youth aesthetic that emphasized conformity and emotional expression. The Bobby-Soxer phenomenon signaled a crucial shift in American society, establishing teenagers as a major distinct consumer demographic. [ 1 ]

They are often retrospectively considered a "patient zero" for intense modern fandom, with their devotion to Frank Sinatra drawing contemporary comparisons to later phenomena such as 1960s Beatlemania and the "Swifties" fandom surrounding Taylor Swift.
culturalContext: Key values (per the Aesthetics Wiki): Peer conformity, emotional release (swooning), consumer autonomy, rejection of formal adult attire
